problem:
Consider the function $f(x),$ defined as follows:

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}{e}^{x}+{x}^{2}+x, & x\le 1 \\ x+a, & 1<x<3 \\ {x}^{2}-2x, & x\ge 3\end{aligned}
$$

Earlier part 1:

It is known that $f$ is continuous at $x=1.$ Find the value of $a.$

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        $a=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        $e+1$

Current part:

${lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{x}^{3}+2}{f(x)}=$

                            
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}

feedback.worked_solution:
We're told that $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=1.$ According to the definition of continuity, this means that ${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)$ exists.

In order for ${lim}_{x\to 1}f(x)$ to exist, the left- and right-sided limits must both exist and be equal.

- Approaching from the left, we have $x<1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)={e}^{x}+{x}^{2}+x.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}({e}^{x}+{x}^{2}+x) \\  & ={e}^{1}+{1}^{2}+1 \\  & =e+2.\end{aligned}
$$

- Approaching from the right, we have $x>1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=x+a.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}(x+a) \\  & =1+a.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the left and right-sided limits must be equal, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x) \\ 1+a & =e+2 \\ a & =e+1.\end{aligned}
$$
